problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934289/assets/e13e109301fca50036cbf933b2a7946f3f53397f39f5e249c0d64e1f6ae78ba2.png)

Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${q}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})$ where $q(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{q}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{q}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{{f}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})\cdot g(\frac{3}{2})-f(\frac{3}{2})\cdot {g}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})}{{(g(\frac{3}{2}))}^{2}}.
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(\frac{3}{2})=1$ and $g(\frac{3}{2})=-1.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $0.$ So, ${f}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})=0.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $1.$ So, ${g}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})=1.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(\frac{3}{2}) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})\cdot g(\frac{3}{2})-f(\frac{3}{2})\cdot {g}^{′}(\frac{3}{2})}{{(g(\frac{3}{2}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The quotient rule for derivatives gives

q′(x)=f′(x)⋅g(x)−f(x)⋅g′(x)(g(x))2.

As a result, we have that

q′(32)=f′(32)⋅g(32)−f(32)⋅g′(32)(g(32))2.

From the graph above, we obtain that f(32)=1 and g(32)=−1.

Additionally:

  • The slope of f(x) on x∈(1,3) equals 0. So, f′(32)=0.

  • The slope of g(x) on x∈(1,3) equals 1. So, g′(32)=1.

Finally, we have

q′(32)=f′(32)⋅g(32)−f(32)⋅g′(32)(g(32))2=0⋅(−1)−1⋅1(−1)2=−1.
